summary: This document updates RFC 6020 and amends IANA guidance on the uniqueness of YANG module and submodule names. It clarifies how modules and their revisions are handled by IANA.

plainLanguage.summary: Every first version of a YANG module gets a name of its own. Later versions of the same module reuse that name, and this document changes the official rule so it says exactly that.

questions: do yang module revisions keep the same name
subtitle: Only the first version of a YANG module needs a unique name; later revisions keep that name and namespace.

tldr.problem: RFC 6020 told IANA that every YANG module and submodule name in its registry must be unique, but in practice a module and all of its revisions share one name, so the written rule did not match what IANA did.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC replaces that text so that only the name and XML namespace of an initial version must be unique, while every revision must keep the name and namespace of the initial version.
tldr.outcome: The written rule now matches IANA's practice, and this document is listed as an additional reference for the YANG Module Names registry.

facts.label: Revisions
facts.value: Must reuse the initial name and namespace

today: RFC 9890 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 6020. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: A Rule That Did Not Match Practice
sections.content:
RFC 6020 created a registry called "YANG Module Names" for the names of YANG modules and submodules. Section 14 of that RFC says every module and submodule name in the registry MUST be unique.

This document reports that the way IANA runs the registry does not follow that guidance, and amends Section 14 so the rule describes what IANA actually does with a module and its revisions.
sections.plainLanguage: The old rule said every name must be different from every other name. In practice, a new version of a module reuses the old name, so the rule needed correcting.

sections.title: The Replacement Rule
sections.content:
The document prints the old text and the new text side by side. The old text required uniqueness for all module and submodule names and all XML namespaces. The new text separates an initial version from its revisions.

  • Modules and their revisions are both kept in the registry.
  • All initial version module and submodule names MUST be unique.
  • All XML namespaces of initial version modules MUST be unique.
  • Every module and submodule revision MUST have the same name as the initial version.
  • Every module revision MUST have the same XML namespace as the initial version.
sections.plainLanguage: Only the first version of a module needs a brand-new name and its own namespace. Every later revision must repeat both of them exactly.

sections.title: Registry and Operational Notes
sections.content:
IANA has updated the "YANG Module Names" registry, which sits under the "YANG Parameters" registry group, to list this document as an additional reference. The RFC says this is needed because its procedure is now the authority for assigning names there.

The document states that it introduces no new operations or manageability requirements and no new or increased security risks. Its text was originally part of a YANG author guidelines document.
sections.plainLanguage: The registry now points to this document as the rule to follow. Nothing else about running a network changes.

cells: Old: XML namespaces MUST be unique
New: revisions MUST reuse name and namespace
